title: Research: rule out seven-owner centre information compression
body:
This adds the first uncovered support case to the selected PR1094 centre-repair information audit. For the pinned calls 0/4 routes and the full later-query observation contract, blocks of up to seven owners still require exactly 104 additional scalar linear observations per owner.

At support seven, the incidence constraints force the Fano plane. The exact census compares all 1,379,952 reduced length-three route products across the 112 pinned involutions. Its 50 non-singleton product classes all have size two, yielding 50 cyclically reduced length-six relations; each is a braid relation, and the resulting route-label graph has no triangles. The Fano incidence would require a triangle, so support seven is impossible. Combined with the predecessor's size-1–6 result, this gives the stated repair minimum through size seven.

This is a scoped information result only. It does not change recursive rank, provide a priced repair, admit a supplier, alter the selected frontier, or improve κ; the requested κ > 0.1 remains unmet. The package stops further centre-block search until a complete replacement endpoint passes the exact κ=0.1 optimistic moment with positive headroom for physical costs.

Validation passed on Python 3.12:

- `python3.12 -I -B research/centre-seven-owner-information-floor/verify.py`
- `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre-seven-owner-information-floor --check-only`
- `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre-seven-owner-information-floor`
- `python3.12 scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/centre-seven-owner-information-floor`

The investigation continues in [Discussion #3062](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/3062). The package retains predecessor attribution and discloses substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.
